title: Uttaradhyayana Sutra
attributionNote: A compilation of older material drawn from the tradition of Mahāvīra's teaching, framed in the voice of his disciple Sudharman. No single author is recorded, and the last lecture is a later addition.
description: The most widely read of the Śvetāmbara scriptures after the Kalpa Sūtra: thirty-six lectures in verse, on discipline, the hardships of the ascetic life, the four requisites, death, the false ascetic, the parable of the ram, the pravrajyā of King Nami, the leaf of the tree, the very learned monk, the true monk, the ten conditions of chastity, the nature of karman, the leśyās, the houseless monk, and the road of penance. Its stories and similes made it the standard primer of Jain doctrine.
historicalContext: The Uttarādhyayana is not one of the twelve Aṅgas but an independent collection, quoted by both Śvetāmbara and Digambara authors and translated early into several Indian languages. Its thirty-sixth lecture, a summary of the whole, is generally recognised as a later supplement.
availabilityNote: Streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive view by view at read time. Jacobi's 1895 translation is public domain; the Prakrit text is not included.
